A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OrcaLoca and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. The original competing-method appendix is retained as Appendix G in v2, with a new cost-analysis Appendix F.

before.justification: Tables 1–3 report original localization and repair results on SWE-bench Lite, an Agentless reproduction, and component ablations on SWE-bench Common.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, supplemented by batching cost measurements in Appendix F and a reported issue-reproduction success rate in Appendix C.

M1.justification: V1 describes single-action execution and agent-generated final locations. Section 5 of v2 introduces optional batched execution and final selection from top-k stored search results. The scheduling, decomposition, and pruning components remain unchanged; the renamed reproducer already existed in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate on SWE-bench Lite and its 93-instance SWE-bench Common subset. The ten issues used for the new cost study are sampled from retained coverage. Other programming languages remain future work.

E2.justification: V1 reports OrcaLoca's search and editing costs without a comparative cost table. V2 Table 4 adds cost comparisons against OpenHands, SWE-Agent, AutoCodeRover, and Agentless-1.5. These methods already participate in the unchanged accuracy comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix F adds a cost experiment comparing ordinary execution with batch size two on ten sampled SWE-bench Lite issues. The original accuracy evaluation retains its model, temperatures, patch-generation budget, metrics, and dataset sizes.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds a cost breakdown and an analysis of whether batching priority-queue actions reduces localization expense, with per-issue comparisons in Table 5. The original component ablations and unique-localization analysis remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix F introduces estimation using weighted averages across cost bins from ten sampled issues. V1 only reports approximate per-instance costs. The new estimator's weights are unspecified, and no confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run uncertainty reporting are added.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their results, including 65.33% function matching and 41.00% issue resolution. V2 adds 38.0% reproduction success and the cost results in Tables 4–5, including an estimated 34% localization-cost reduction from 0.87 to 0.58 under batching. This is a new configuration comparison, not an improvement in the retained accuracy results.

T1.justification: The graph and state definitions, distance heuristic, matching metrics, and Appendix E convergence criterion are retained. The initial-state notation edit and new pseudocode do not introduce a new theoretical result, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same three central contributions and the same claims of 65.33% function matching and a 6.33-percentage-point resolution improvement through Agentless integration.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds concrete qualifications concerning Python-specific parsing, cross-language support, alternative LLMs, system overhead, and batching tradeoffs. Appendix C explicitly frames reproduction as complementary because only 38.0% of issues were reproduced. The interpretations of the main accuracy results remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The advertised code location changes from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository. V2 also documents on-demand shortest-path computation, graph reconstruction per repository and commit, and reproducer-derived initial actions. Existing API descriptions, prompts, and core hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to the Qwen3 technical report and LLaMA when discussing prospective model support. The existing related-work discussion and positioning against software-engineering agents remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 inserts a Discussion section and Cost Breakdown Analysis appendix, renames Appendix C to Reproducer Agent, and renumbers the conclusion and competing-method appendix. Local explanations and acknowledgments expand, while most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Algorithm 1 and two cost tables. Existing figures and tables shift with text reflow, including Figure 3 and Tables 2–3; Figure 5 receives a revised caption. The original visual content and principal table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency about reproduction failures, applicability limits, and efficiency through the expanded discussion and inspectable cost measurements. The gain is limited: the main validation is unchanged, cost estimates rely on ten issues with unspecified weights, and Algorithm 1 initializes an empty queue before requiring it to be nonempty to enter the loop. The added practical evidence and qualifications nevertheless provide a modest net improvement.
